(a) The McMahon line deﬁ nes the boundary between India and China. It was agreed on under Shimla Accord, a treaty signed in 1914 (Agreed between Britain and Tibet). The line is named after Sir Henry McMahon, foreign secretary of the British-run Government of India and the chief negotiator of the convention at Shimla. The line was drawn 500 miles east of Bhutan. India considers this line as a permanent national border while China considers the line as a temporary line of control. China even does not consider the Shimla Pact. 6. (c) Radcliffe line defines the boundary between India and Pakistan. The 38th parallel line deﬁ nes the boundary between North Korea and South Korea and the 49th parallel line deﬁ nes the boundary between the United States of America and Canada. Similarly, the Mac Mahon line deﬁ nes the boundary between India and China. 7. 38th Parallel border lines divide which of the two following countries?
